note: Tier-3 generic passthrough adapter for Google's Antigravity CLI (`agy`), the second route of the Gemini pilot (2AMLogic/2am docs/llm-policy.md rule 6; issue #14945). worktreeIsolation and loomControl are declared 'no' EXPLICITLY: Builder and Doctor (both requirements) and Judge (loomControl) are refused by the same check-runtime-capabilities.sh mechanism that keeps every other tier-3 runtime out of worktree-mutating roles, so the pilot is read-only roles only (Curator, Guide, Auditor). Unlike every other tier-3 runtime this manifest declares a credential pool: `credentialPool: gemini` + `credentialEnv: GEMINI_API_KEY` make `loom-daemon spawn-worker` draw the key from the gemini API-key account pool IN THE WORKER PROCESS and hand it to the child environment only — the pool is MANDATORY (a missing, unreadable, disabled, exhausted or at-cap pool refuses the launch at 78 even when an ambient GEMINI_API_KEY or cached Google login exists), because the account's maxConcurrent cap is the pilot's spend control and is shared with OpenCode's quick-flash profile through the same `gemini` namespace. An ambient GEMINI_API_KEY never reaches the child: the pool's selection replaces it. `model` is the pilot's default (the 2026-11-22 canary's `gemini-4-neon`, agy 1.5.14); LOOM_MODEL overrides it (env > manifest) and is passed to the CLI exactly once via launch.modelFlag. Effort is deliberately not mapped: the canary could not tell which effort level a bare model name selects, and `agy models` lists -low/medium/high/xhigh variants an operator can pass through explicitly. The `--settings <isolated>/settings.json` + `--sandbox` argv come from spawn-agy.sh, not from launch.extraArgs, because the settings path is per-launch (a fresh isolated HOME that also defeats agy's cached-login path); `--sandbox` is the guarded permission choice over the auto-approve flag. The settings/update flag surface must be re-verified against the pinned binary — see defaults/docs/runtime-adapters.md's agy section for the 1.5.14 pin, the update-control requirement and the live-verification tracking issue.
